patch.value: Context relevance re-ranker with usage-affinity learning loop

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Design: register governed context_relevance service override that nudges pm's default ranking with a recency-decayed usage affinity derived from an append-only JSONL ledger at runtime/context-usage.jsonl. Auto-touch loop reads previous serve row + history/*.jsonl (ts field) to record touches for served items mutated since the last serve. New pm context-usage command for inspection/manual touch/reset. Fail-open returns undefined on any error.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Acceptance criteria: (1) context_relevance service registered via api.registerService returning {id,score}[] for every candidate. (2) Ledger at runtime/context-usage.jsonl bounded to 2000 rows, corrupt lines skipped. (3) Affinity in [0,1], neutral for unseen items, served-but-untouched below unserved. (4) Auto-touch from previous serve row + history ts. (5) pm context-usage command with --report/--touch/--reset/--json/--limit/--pm-path. (6) Fail-open returns undefined, never throws. (7) 100% coverage of new code. (8) manifest.json services capability added. (9) Four functional proofs in /tmp workspace.

patch.value: pm context-usage: report which served context an agent actually used

value.author: claude
value.text: SCOPE CHANGE. The original design (a governed context_relevance service override plus a hand-rolled usage ledger) was discarded before implementation because it duplicated and would have corrupted shipped pm behaviour. pm 2026.7.25 already maintains runtime/context-usage.jsonl itself and already folds it into the usage_affinity signal of its built-in relevance model. The discarded draft wrote to that exact filename with an incompatible row schema ({t,at,id} vs pms {kind,at,author,item_id,intent}), so two writers with two schemas would have silently corrupted the signal both depend on.

value.author: claude
value.text: DELIVERED: read-only pm context-usage. Reports serve-then-touch conversion, waste (served but never touched = context paid for and unused) and misses (touched but never served = ranking failed to surface it), plus a per-item rollup. Deliberately does NOT compute a competing affinity score: pm owns the decay model, and a second implementation could silently disagree with the ranking it claims to explain. Flags: --author --surface --since --limit --format; the global --json is honoured.

value.author: claude
value.text: Acceptance: (1) 100/100/100/100 coverage on context-usage.ts via c8. (2) Registration and command execution tested through the SDKs own host harness (activateExtensionForTest / createExtensionTestHarness) instead of hand-built api doubles, so manifest capability governance is enforced in tests. (3) Verified against the real CLI on a live tracker: 33.3% conversion, 3 waste items, filters and rc=2 usage errors all correct. (4) index.ts api/ctx now typed with SDK ExtensionApi and CommandHandlerContext instead of any.

value.author: claude
value.text: Upstream issues filed from this work: pm-cli#717 (extensions cannot import the runtime SDK; ExtensionCommandSdk is the right mechanism but omits the derived-state readers) and pm-cli#719 (extension flags colliding with a pm global flag are silently shadowed - found by real-CLI testing after unit tests passed against a permissive double).

value.author: claude
value.text: CodeRabbit review round 1 found two real defects, both fixed. P1: serves counted every ranked row, so an item pm ranked but cut from the pack was reported as waste - contradicting the modules own stated semantics, and my test had codified the wrong result. Now serves counts only included rows and a separate ranked column exposes budget losses (ranked - serves). P2: parseLedgerLine validated at as a string only, while every window filter, bound and conversion check compares timestamps lexically; "...00.500Z" sorts BEFORE "...00Z" because . precedes Z, so a non-canonical spelling silently inverted chronological order. Now requires canonical toISOString form.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Acceptance scenario against the built package and a real scratch tracker before source changes: serve two focus facts in session-a; cite the first, then measure one used of two served facts (precision 0.5), positive unused estimated token cost, and no attribution to session-b. Baseline selects both items but has no context_receipt and no bundle/session metrics. Implement stable section/fact ids for the actually rendered subset, isolated bounded runtime receipts, explicit citation/item/file usage reports, session-aware later SDK touches, and README agent protocol. Existing notes describe the shipped legacy read-only report; the requested receipt measurement extends it without a competing relevance service or host-ledger schema.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Implemented the v1 receipt protocol on both serving paths. Facts are derived after rendering so omitted sections and truncated body text stay outside the denominator. Explicit receipt-scoped citations, successful item-mutation reports and file-edit reports are idempotent and session isolated; estimates disclose four-character token approximation and proxy limitations. Storage uses bounded atomic runtime snapshots separate from the SDK ledger. Built-package acceptance passes for two focus facts, one citation, precision 0.5 and an untouched independent session. The SDK touch ledger lacks session/fact ids and a generic fact-level post-egress callback, so hooks report usage explicitly and complete file delivery is documented.
